h: Know the Lingo Before You Bowl
p: Every group has one person who suddenly starts talking like a pro after a single strike, so here's how to keep up. A strike is all ten pins down with the first ball of a frame. A spare means you cleared the rest with your second. Three strikes on the trot is a turkey, and an open frame is when pins are still standing after both balls. A gutter ball needs no explanation, and you'll likely see a few.

Beginner tips are simple: choose a ball you can comfortably swing, aim for the arrows on the lane rather than the pins, and follow through straight. Don't step over the foul line, as it costs you the shot.

Beyond the city centre spots, Leeds has more to offer. Roundhay Park is a huge green space on the north side of the city, with lakes, woodland and Tropical World, a warm glasshouse full of creatures and plants. Leeds Art Gallery and the Henry Moore Institute sit side by side on The Headrow, and the domed Corn Exchange is a gorgeous Victorian building full of independent shops. A short drive out, Harewood House offers a grand country estate with gardens and grounds to explore.

Leeds railway station is right in the city centre and well connected, making it a convenient spot for groups travelling in from across Yorkshire. Sort a meeting point in advance and get there a little early so nobody is still looking for the venue when the first ball rolls.
